# A grid column renderer from an ancestor runs with the column as this, so examples/grid/cellEditing renders nothing

## Context

`examples/grid/cellEditing` renders **no rows at all**. Measured on `dev@d486a03a8d` by loading `/examples/grid/cellEditing/index.html` in Chromium: `0` elements match `.neo-grid-cell`, and the App Worker logs

```
vdom update failed neo-grid-body-1 TypeError: this.getStateProvider is not a function
    at Column.countryRenderer (examples/grid/cellEditing/MainContainer.mjs:34:33)
    at Row.applyRendererOutput (src/grid/Row.mjs:190:42)
```

`Column.countryRenderer` is the tell: the method is defined on `Neo.examples.grid.cellEditing.MainContainer` and reached through `renderer: 'up.countryRenderer'`, but it runs with the **column** as `this`.

This is a regression of #6620, which fixed exactly this example:

| commit | date | scope the renderer is called with |
|---|---|---|
| `dd4572d8d5` (#6620) | 2025-04-05 | `column.rendererScope \|\| me` — `me` was `grid.View`, the caller |
| `f691b3faf0` (#8970, Row pooling) | 2026-02-03 | `column.rendererScope \|\| column` — reintroduced in the new `grid/Row.mjs` |

The Row-pooling refactor moved `applyRendererOutput` from `grid.View` into `Neo.grid.Row` and restored the pre-#6620 default on the way.

## The Problem

Two independent losses put the ancestor's method on the column's `this`:

1. **`grid.column.Base#beforeSetRenderer` (`src/grid/column/Base.mjs:219`)** calls `resolveCallback(value, this)` and keeps only `.fn`:

   ```js
   return resolveCallback(value, this).fn || value
   ```

   `resolveCallback` (`src/util/Function.mjs:158-171`) returns `{fn, scope}` and, for an `up.` name, walks the parent chain until it finds the owner — `{fn: MainContainer.prototype.countryRenderer, scope: theMainContainer}`. The scope it found is dropped on the floor.

2. **`grid.Row#applyRendererOutput` (`src/grid/Row.mjs:190`)** then supplies its own default:

   ```js
   rendererOutput = column.renderer.call(column.rendererScope || column, rendererConfig)
   ```

   So a renderer that came from an ancestor is invoked with the column. `Neo.grid.column.Base` has no `getStateProvider`, and the render throws inside the body's update — which is why the grid renders nothing rather than one bad cell.

The default renderer is unaffected and must stay that way: `renderer_: 'cellRenderer'` (`src/grid/column/Base.mjs:73`) resolves on the column itself, so `resolveCallback` returns the column as scope, which is correct.

## The Architectural Reality

| surface | today |
|---|---|
| `src/util/Function.mjs:158` `resolveCallback` | returns `{fn, scope}`; `up.` walks `scope.parent` until the name resolves |
| `src/grid/column/Base.mjs:219` `beforeSetRenderer` | keeps `.fn`, discards `.scope` |
| `src/grid/column/Base.mjs:81` `rendererScope` | `{Neo.core.Base\|String\|null}`, the designed home for a scope |
| `src/grid/Row.mjs:172` | `rendererScope` `'me'`/`'this'` means the column — `grid.column.Component` (`:55`) relies on it |
| `src/grid/Row.mjs:190`/`:196` | calls `renderer` and `extraCls` with `column.rendererScope \|\| column` |
| `src/table/Body.mjs:175` | the Table sibling defaults to `tableContainer`, never the column |
| `src/table/header/Button.mjs:228` | discards `.scope` the same way; Table's container default hides it |

## The Fix

- **`grid.column.Base#beforeSetRenderer` keeps the scope it resolved.** When `resolveCallback` returns a scope that is not the column and `rendererScope` is unset, the column records it, so an `up.` renderer runs on the instance that defines it — the whole point of `up.`.
- **`grid.Row#applyRendererOutput` defaults to the grid Container**, not the column, for both `renderer` and `extraCls`, restoring #6620's contract in today's topology and matching `table/Body.mjs:175`.
- `rendererScope: 'me' | 'this'` keeps meaning the column.
- Anchor & Echo JSDoc on `rendererScope` and `beforeSetRenderer` stating which scope wins, in which order.

## Contract Ledger

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Neo.grid.column.Base#renderer_` string resolution | `src/grid/column/Base.mjs:219` | an `up.` name keeps the ancestor `resolveCallback` found as its scope | a name found on the column keeps the column, as today | config JSDoc | unit arm, red on `dev` |
| `Neo.grid.column.Base#rendererScope` | `src/grid/column/Base.mjs:81` | explicit config still wins over everything; `'me'`/`'this'` still means the column | unchanged | config JSDoc | unit arm |
| `Neo.grid.Row#applyRendererOutput` default scope | `src/grid/Row.mjs:190`, `:196` | the grid Container, as `table/Body.mjs:175` does | a column with `rendererScope` is unaffected | method JSDoc | unit arm + the example arm |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1** — a grid column with `renderer: 'up.someMethod'`, where `someMethod` lives on an ancestor, invokes it with that ancestor as `this` (red on `dev`).
- [ ] **AC-2** — a grid column with a plain function `renderer` and no `rendererScope` invokes it with the grid Container as `this` (red on `dev`).
- [ ] **AC-3** — `rendererScope: 'me'` and `'this'` still invoke with the column, and the default `cellRenderer` still resolves on the column: `grid.column.Component` keeps rendering.
- [ ] **AC-4** — `examples/grid/cellEditing` renders its rows with no page error and no App Worker error (red on `dev`: 0 cells, `this.getStateProvider is not a function`).
- [ ] **AC-5** — a function `cellCls` follows the same scope rule as `renderer` (`src/grid/Row.mjs:196` applies the same default).
- [ ] **AC-6** — coverage CI executes: unit arms for AC-1, 2, 3, 5 and a components-tier arm for AC-4.

## Out of Scope

`table.header.Button#beforeSetRenderer`, which drops the same scope — Table's container default hides it, and Table is a separate control. Recorded here; file it separately if a Table renderer needs its owner. · The cell-editing feature itself (#18762, #18764). · Any renderer API beyond scope resolution.

## Avoided Traps

- **Defaulting to the Row.** The Row is a pooled projection; a renderer holding it would hold a slot, not the grid.
- **Only changing the Row default.** It fixes this example by accident — the container happens to have `getStateProvider` — and still runs an ancestor's method with the wrong `this` the moment the method touches its own members.
- **Resolving the string per render.** `beforeSetRenderer` resolves once at config time; per-render resolution would put a parent-chain walk in the pooled render path.
